$comment: The lifecycle half of 'may a reader see this article', written once and run
twice: by ge.magti.portal.article.ArticleVisibilityParityTest against
ArticleVisibility.java, and by article-visibility.spec.ts against
angular-frontend/src/app/shared/article-visibility.ts.
Only the clause both sides actually evaluate is listed here -- status,
publishedAt and isDraft. The backend additionally decides audience
(DepartmentMatcher) and lets content administrators through; that is not
duplicated between the two and so is not compared here.
isDraft is optional and defaults to false, which is what every case
written before 2026-09-06 means. It joined this fixture the day
ArticleVisibility.java was found not to evaluate it at all: the lists were
right because their SQL carries the rule separately, but /uploads and the
note endpoints ask this rule directly and got the weaker answer. The one
case the two sides cannot share is the author's own draft -- the frontend
surfaces have no author to compare against -- so that stays in
ArticleVisibilityDraftTest on the Java side.
publishedAt is relative on purpose. The backend compares against
TbilisiTime.now() (a fixed +04:00 offset) and the browser against the
viewer's local clock, so the two agree for a viewer in Georgia and can
differ by hours for one elsewhere. Every case below is a full day either
side of now, which keeps the fixture about the rule rather than about the
clock. That boundary difference is real and deliberate -- the product is
Georgia-only -- but it is the reason not to add a 'one second ago' case.

cases.name: published, with no date at all
cases.why: published short-circuits before the date is looked at

cases.name: published, with a future date
cases.why: same short-circuit; status wins over a stale future date

cases.name: scheduled, moment has passed
cases.why: nothing flips the status column, so the date is the truth

cases.name: scheduled, with no date
cases.why: a schedule with no moment never arrives

cases.name: an unrecognised status
cases.why: both sides allow-list rather than deny-list, so a new status is invisible until it is handled

cases.name: somebody else's autosave draft that says published
cases.why: is_draft is the personal-autosave flag and outranks status; this exact pair was readable through /uploads until 2026-09-06

cases.name: somebody else's autosave draft that is scheduled and due
cases.why: the draft clause is evaluated before the date, so a due schedule cannot publish a private draft
